findings.message: This change makes a completed release final: `tag_release` and `set_release_proposals` now go through `openRelease` and refuse it, and the release page hides its re-tag and change-proposals buttons. `releaseOffers` was not changed. It still offers both to any release that isn't live in Prod, so a completed Dev or UAT release offers two writes that can only fail. Fix: drop the 'Change the proposals' and 'Re-tag' offers when the release's status is `completed`. Add a variant test that covers a completed Dev release, a completed UAT release and an open one.
findings.scenario: Release RTK d1 (category UAT) completes on a UAT deployment. Pin it in chat: the offers include 'Re-tag RTK d1' and 'Change the proposals in RTK d1'. Confirming either one is refused with 'RTK d1 is completed; it can't change'.

findings.message: `categoryEnv` finds a Dev or UAT release's completing environment by matching the name at deployment time (`lower(name) = 'dev'|'uat'`). The name is only checked when the release is created or edited (`categoryProblem`). After that, `upsert_environment` can rename the environment and `remove_environment` can delete it (when it has no deployments), and neither checks for open releases of that category. From then on, `completeOnDeployment` finds no environment and returns null without saying anything. The release can never complete, and the hourly check moves it to Off track and notifies the PM. Fix: resolve the category to an environment id once and store it on the release (e.g. `category_environment_id`), and complete against that id. Otherwise, have upsertEnvironment and removeEnvironment refuse to rename or delete an environment that an open release's category depends on. Never treat a missing environment as 'not this deployment'.
findings.scenario: Create RTK release r1 with category UAT. upsert_environment {projectKey: RTK, name: UAT, rename: Staging}. record_deployment r1 to Staging, status deployed → r1 stays in_progress. After its target day, the check sets it to overdue and Maya gets 'r1 is now Off track', even though the release did ship to that environment.

findings.message: A release completes only inside `recordDeployment`, when a new deployment arrives. `updateRelease` sets status through `statusFor`, which always passes `completed: false`. It ignores deployed records the release already has in the category's environment. Two cases go wrong. Tracking an older release that is already live (the 'Ask amax to track it' path), and changing a release's category to an environment it has already deployed to, both leave the release in_progress or overdue. Neither will ever complete without a fake redeploy, and an overdue result sends a false Off track notice. Fix: when `updateRelease` sets or changes the category, look up the latest live `deployed` record in that environment and complete through the same `completeBy` path. Add a variant test for both cases: tracking an untracked live release, and switching category to one already reached.
findings.scenario: CON v2.4.0 (untracked) already has a live deployed Prod record. update_release {category: prod, startDate: 2026-09-01, targetDate: 2026-09-30} → status overdue (not completed), a 'v2.4.0 is now Off track' notice goes to the PM, and it stays Off track forever.

findings.message: The new `delivery.release-off-track` rule has no `except`, and `ReleaseStatusChanged` carries no `by`. When the PM's own edit moves the release to overdue (`update_release` with a target in the past, or `create_release` with one), the PM gets an urgent notice about their own action. The other Delivery owner rules leave out the person who acted (`except: "by"`). Fix: add `by` to the payload for create and update sources (null for schedule) and set `except: "by"`.
findings.scenario: Maya (PM of CON) runs update_release CON v9 targetDate=2026-11-01 when today is 2026-11-26 → Maya gets the urgent notice 'v9 is now Off track' for the change she just made.
